title.en: I was walking when it started
title.de: Die Verlaufsform der Vergangenheit: I was walking
title.it: Il passato progressivo: I was walking

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj se je ravno dogajalo (I was walking), kaj se je zgodilo medtem (when it started to rain, while I was cooking), in vprašaš What were you doing?
goal.de: Du sagst, was gerade los war (I was walking) und was dabei passierte (when it started to rain, while I was cooking), und fragst What were you doing?
goal.it: Dici che cosa stava succedendo (I was walking) e che cosa è successo intanto (when it started to rain, while I was cooking), e chiedi What were you doing?
goal.en: You can say what was going on (I was walking), what happened meanwhile (when it started to rain, while I was cooking), and ask What were you doing?

say.sl: Ko poveš, kaj se je ravno dogajalo v nekem trenutku v preteklosti, rečeš **was** ali **were** + glagol z **-ing**: **I was walking.** (Ravno sem hodil{m:|f:a}.) **Jack was shearing.** (Jack je ravno strigel.) **We were working.** (Ravno smo delali.) Slovenščina to pove z nedovršnim glagolom.
say.de: Um zu sagen, was in einem Moment der Vergangenheit gerade los war, nimmst du **was** oder **were** + Verb mit **-ing**: **I was walking.** (Ich ging gerade.) **Jack was shearing.** (Jack schor gerade.) **We were working.** (Wir arbeiteten gerade.) Wie das present continuous, nur mit was und were.
say.it: Per dire che cosa stava succedendo in un momento del passato usi **was** o **were** + il verbo in **-ing**: **I was walking.** (Stavo camminando.) **Jack was shearing.** (Jack stava tosando.) **We were working.** (Stavamo lavorando.) È come stare + gerundio al passato.
say.en: To say what was going on at a moment in the past, use **was** or **were** + the verb with **-ing**: **I was walking.** **Jack was shearing.** **We were working.** It is the present continuous with was and were.

examples.sl: Ob desetih sem ravno hodil{m:|f:a} proti gostilni.
examples.de: Um zehn Uhr ging ich gerade zum Gasthaus.
examples.it: Alle dieci stavo camminando verso la locanda.

say.sl: Zanikanje je **wasn't** ali **weren't**: **It wasn't raining.** (Ni deževalo.) **They weren't listening.** (Niso poslušali.) Za vprašanje gre was ali were na začetek: **Were you sleeping?** (Si ravno spal{m:|f:a}?) **What were you doing?** (Kaj si ravno delal{m:|f:a}?) **Yes, I was.** **No, I wasn't.** Nikoli *Did you sleeping?*
say.de: Verneint heißt es **wasn't** oder **weren't**: **It wasn't raining.** (Es regnete nicht.) **They weren't listening.** (Sie hörten nicht zu.) In der Frage kommt was oder were nach vorn: **Were you sleeping?** (Hast du gerade geschlafen?) **What were you doing?** (Was hast du gerade gemacht?) **Yes, I was.** **No, I wasn't.** Nie *Did you sleeping?*
say.it: La negazione è **wasn't** o **weren't**: **It wasn't raining.** (Non pioveva.) **They weren't listening.** (Non stavano ascoltando.) Per chiedere, was o were va all'inizio: **Were you sleeping?** (Stavi dormendo?) **What were you doing?** (Che cosa stavi facendo?) **Yes, I was.** **No, I wasn't.** Mai *Did you sleeping?*
say.en: For no, say **wasn't** or **weren't**: **It wasn't raining.** **They weren't listening.** To ask, was or were goes first: **Were you sleeping?** **What were you doing?** **Yes, I was.** **No, I wasn't.** Never *Did you sleeping?*

say.sl: Glavna raba je z **when** (ko): **I was walking when it started to rain.** (Ravno sem hodil{m:|f:a}, ko je začelo deževati.) Dolgo dejanje je z **-ing**, kratko v *past simple*. **We were eating when Sam came in.** (Ravno smo jedli, ko je vstopil Sam.)
say.de: Das Wichtigste ist **when** (als): **I was walking when it started to rain.** (Ich ging gerade, als es zu regnen begann.) Das Lange steht mit **-ing**, das Kurze im *past simple*. **We were eating when Sam came in.** (Wir aßen gerade, als Sam hereinkam.)
say.it: L'uso principale è con **when** (quando): **I was walking when it started to rain.** (Stavo camminando quando ha cominciato a piovere.) Il fatto lungo va in **-ing**, quello breve al *past simple*. **We were eating when Sam came in.** (Stavamo mangiando quando è entrato Sam.)
say.en: The main use is with **when**: **I was walking when it started to rain.** The long one takes **-ing**, the short one the past simple. **We were eating when Sam came in.**

say.sl: **while** (medtem ko) gre z dolgim dejanjem, z **-ing**: **While I was cooking, the phone rang.** (Medtem ko sem kuhal{m:|f:a}, je zazvonil telefon.) **The phone rang while I was cooking.** Dve dolgi dejanji hkrati: **While Jack was shearing, Meg was sleeping.** (Medtem ko je Jack strigel, je Meg spala.) Nikoli *during I was cooking*.
say.de: **while** (während) steht beim Langen, mit **-ing**: **While I was cooking, the phone rang.** (Während ich kochte, klingelte das Telefon.) **The phone rang while I was cooking.** Zwei lange Dinge zugleich: **While Jack was shearing, Meg was sleeping.** (Während Jack schor, schlief Meg.) Nie *during I was cooking*.
say.it: **while** (mentre) va con il fatto lungo, in **-ing**: **While I was cooking, the phone rang.** (Mentre cucinavo, è squillato il telefono.) **The phone rang while I was cooking.** Due fatti lunghi insieme: **While Jack was shearing, Meg was sleeping.** (Mentre Jack tosava, Meg dormiva.) Mai *during I was cooking*.
say.en: **while** goes with the long one, with **-ing**: **While I was cooking, the phone rang.** **The phone rang while I was cooking.** Two long things at once: **While Jack was shearing, Meg was sleeping.** Never *during I was cooking*.

say.sl: Pravopis je kot v sedanjiku: make → **making**, sit → **sitting**, lie → **lying**. Glagoli za stanja tudi tu nimajo -ing: **know**, **like**, **want**, **need**: **I knew the way.** (Poznal{m:|f:a} sem pot.) Nikoli *I was knowing the way*. **She wanted a cup of tea.** (Hotela je skodelico čaja.)
say.de: Die Schreibung ist wie im Präsens: make → **making**, sit → **sitting**, lie → **lying**. Verben für Zustände bekommen auch hier kein -ing: **know**, **like**, **want**, **need**: **I knew the way.** (Ich kannte den Weg.) Nie *I was knowing the way*. **She wanted a cup of tea.** (Sie wollte eine Tasse Tee.)
say.it: L'ortografia è come al presente: make → **making**, sit → **sitting**, lie → **lying**. I verbi di stato non prendono -ing neanche qui: **know**, **like**, **want**, **need**: **I knew the way.** (Conoscevo la strada.) Mai *I was knowing the way*. **She wanted a cup of tea.** (Voleva una tazza di tè.)
say.en: The spelling is as in the present: make → **making**, sit → **sitting**, lie → **lying**. Verbs for states take no -ing here either: **know**, **like**, **want**, **need**: **I knew the way.** Never *I was knowing the way*. **She wanted a cup of tea.**

say.sl: Zgodba se pogosto začne tako, najprej kaj se je dogajalo, potem kaj se je zgodilo: **It was raining and the wind was blowing.** (Deževalo je in pihal je veter.) **Old Wilf was sitting by the fire.** (Stari Wilf je sedel ob ognju.) **Suddenly the door opened.** (Nenadoma so se odprla vrata.) Ozadje z -ing, nov dogodek v *past simple*.
say.de: So beginnt oft eine Geschichte, zuerst was gerade los war, dann was geschah: **It was raining and the wind was blowing.** (Es regnete, und der Wind blies.) **Old Wilf was sitting by the fire.** (Der alte Wilf saß am Feuer.) **Suddenly the door opened.** (Plötzlich ging die Tür auf.) Das Drumherum mit -ing, das Neue im *past simple*.
say.it: Spesso una storia comincia così, prima che cosa stava succedendo, poi che cosa è successo: **It was raining and the wind was blowing.** (Pioveva e soffiava il vento.) **Old Wilf was sitting by the fire.** (Il vecchio Wilf era seduto accanto al fuoco.) **Suddenly the door opened.** (All'improvviso la porta si è aperta.) Lo sfondo in -ing, il fatto nuovo al *past simple*.
say.en: A story often opens this way, first what was going on, then what happened: **It was raining and the wind was blowing.** **Old Wilf was sitting by the fire.** **Suddenly the door opened.** The scene with -ing, the new thing in the past simple.

While Old Wilf ___ (tell) a story, the lights went out! — What ___ you doing, Jack? — I ___ (sit) on the stairs with Meg, but we ___ (not sleep)!

translation.sl: Prejšnji petek je bilo veliko neurje. Ves večer je deževalo in pihal je veter. Gospa Birkett je kuhala v kuhinji, otroci pa so se igrali ob ognju. Medtem ko je stari Wilf pripovedoval zgodbo, je ugasnila luč! — Kaj si pa delal, Jack? — Sedel sem na stopnicah z Meg, ampak nisva spala!
translation.de: Letzten Freitag gab es ein großes Unwetter. Es regnete den ganzen Abend, und der Wind blies. Mrs Birkett kochte in der Küche, und die Kinder spielten am Feuer. Während der alte Wilf eine Geschichte erzählte, ging das Licht aus! — Was hast du gerade gemacht, Jack? — Ich saß mit Meg auf der Treppe, aber wir schliefen nicht!
translation.it: Venerdì scorso c'è stato un grande temporale. Ha piovuto tutta la sera e soffiava il vento. La signora Birkett stava cucinando in cucina e i bambini giocavano accanto al fuoco. Mentre il vecchio Wilf raccontava una storia, è andata via la luce! — Che cosa stavi facendo, Jack? — Ero seduto sulle scale con Meg, ma non dormivamo!
translation.en: Last Friday there was a big storm. It was raining all evening and the wind was blowing. Mrs Birkett was cooking in the kitchen and the children were playing by the fire. While Old Wilf was telling a story, the lights went out! — What were you doing, Jack? — I was sitting on the stairs with Meg, but we weren't sleeping!
